catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries the absolute four-axis stage pose: cap.motion.joint_position.v1 declares joint_positions in radians for every joint, while this controller's X, Y and Z are millimetres and R is degrees, and cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is restricted to robot.arm (this device is motion.axis) and has no rotation axis. The extension keeps each axis in the unit the upstream Position model publishes and lets the runtime enforce per-axis operator envelopes.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/uw-loci__flamingo_control --backend fake (exit 0; all gates G1-G9 pass with no findings; evidence contract_checked, not an MHS-Device level). The card's decision is direct-driver and the package is a direct Driver over py2flamingo.controllers.position_controller:PositionController with a native.py factory; the family helper PythonObjectDriver is not used because the stage needs explicit per-axis units, the native bounds check, the native HALT stop and the reset hook. The other card entry symbols (CommandClient, TCPClient, ConnectionManager, MVCConnectionService) are parts of the application transport and are not this package's device. NOT COVERED: go_home, the relative jogs (jog_x/jog_y/jog_z/jog_rotation), the single-axis moves (move_x/move_y/move_z/move_rotation), set_motion_complete_callback, position history, the preset service, the stage-limit values as read state, a standalone clear_emergency_stop action, and the camera, laser and acquisition parts of the clone. Only the tracked position and home state, the four-axis absolute move, the HALT stop and the e-stop/reset are exposed. No text file of the clone states the stage travel: the limits are loaded per microscope from {microscope_name}_settings.json at run time (configuration_service.py:316-327), so X, Y, Z, R and the four home coordinates are Limit.operator_required and every move or home write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET until the operator's site-limits.json supplies them; site-limits.example.json is an example for one bench, not a statement about any unit. The StageLimits dataclass defaults (models/microscope.py:117-124) are constructor defaults and were deliberately not used as bounds. The move action reports the commanded target, not a measured completion, because the native move sends the command and returns immediately (position_controller.py:294-296); it first calls the controller's is_position_within_bounds because move_to_position silently clamps (position_controller.py:608-625). The stop action ignores the class's optional deceleration because the native HALT command takes no profile. The fake starts at placeholder positions/home and moves instantly; it does not model the asynchronous motion-complete tracker, the movement lock or any hardware timing. Hardware was never attached: native.py and the upstream py2flamingo package were never imported or executed, and no hardware run is claimed. The package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by null) and is R1; the loader's review refusal of a model-written hardware backend applies only at R2 and R3, so the hardware backend remains an operator decision and no protection beyond the SDK is claimed.
